productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Made up animals, non-North American animals, and clear AI flawsMade up animals, non-North American animals, and clear AI flaws
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Junky coloring book with a lot of AI nonsense. There are a several made up animals, and even African antelope species depicted in the book (definitely not North American animals or environments in some of these, as the title suggests). There is what I believe is supposed to be a wild turkey (the head is super not turkey-like, but I literally don't know what else it is, definitely not generic grouse or quail or anything), that clearly has three legs. There's a bison with a... lovecraftian creature in the distance behind it that I imagine is supposed to be another bison, but AI clearly got confused. There's four or five deer pictures but they're kind of just generic "deer" rather than clearly defined species. There are made up bird species rather than normal hunted species (there is one fairly normal duck and some cute quail, but the rest of the birds are not realistic). The pictures themselves all have grayscale shading which some might like, but it prevents you from doing any kind of complex shading yourself. The quality of the images vary from picture to picture. Some have really bold animal outlines, some are more just a shaded image with undefined areas for coloring. A kid might enjoy coloring this book, but I can't imagine an adult or someone genuinely interested in coloring North American game species specifically enjoying this book. I liked the pictures that were shown on the back of the book and they are inside this book, but those four pictures do not represent the bulk of the content of this book. I definitely wouldn't have purchased if I had realized it was AI junk.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Finally, A Coloring Book for People Who Smell Like Deer Season
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this Hunting-Themed Coloring Book for Adults and Teens thinking it would be a casual, relaxing little pastime. What I didn’t expect was to be emotionally invested in a pencil-shaded whitetail while aggressively debating camo color choices like I was planning opening day.First off — the quality is actually solid. The paper is thick enough that my overly enthusiastic “rut-season red” didn’t bleed through to the next page (unless you’re going full Sharpie like a madman). The line work is crisp and detailed without being microscopic. You can actually tell what’s going on in the scenes — which is important when you’re trying to decide whether that’s shadow or “I accidentally colored outside the lines because I got distracted thinking about trail cams.”Now let’s talk about the picture.Yes. The legendary one.The hunter is hanging from the tree.At first glance, I thought, “Wow, bold artistic choice.”At second glance, I thought, “Buddy… we’ve all been there, and I remember this day well!"There’s something deeply relatable about a hunter suspended mid-regret like a human piñata. Is he:• Avoiding a bear?• Testing a questionable tree stand?• Demonstrating upper-body strength he absolutely did not train for?The beauty of this page is that you get to color-commentate the entire scene. I personally went with:• Bright orange for maximum “should’ve worn a harness” energy.• Dramatic forest greens to emphasize the suspense.• A slightly embarrassed blush tone on the hunter’s face because we’ve all made decisions in the woods we don’t talk about.It’s unintentionally hilarious and somehow still wholesome.Overall, this book hits the sweet spot between relaxing art therapy and “why is this so funny?” It’s perfect for hunters, outdoorsmen, or anyone who enjoys quiet evenings coloring wildlife while questioning the life choices of illustrated characters.Would I recommend it? Absolutely.Would I hang from a tree like that? No.Will I be coloring that page again just to try different camo patterns? Also, yes.10/10. Pass the colored pencils, and somebody grab that man a safety harness
